original_question: For every graph G, is the list packing number chi*_l(G) always at most twice the list-chromatic number chi_l(G)? Equivalently, if chi_l(G) is the least k such that every k-list-assignment admits a proper coloring and chi*_l(G) is the least k such that every k-list-assignment admits k pairwise-disjoint proper colorings, must chi*_l(G) <= 2 chi_l(G) hold for all graphs G?
target_in_paper: Section 2, "Various open problems related to list packing," Problem 2.2: "Is it true that χ^*_ℓ(G) ≤ 2χ_ℓ(G) for every graph G?"
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right target exactly: the paper’s Problem 2.2 asks whether the list packing number is always at most twice the list-chromatic number for every graph. You also correctly capture the intended meanings of χ_ℓ(G) and χ^*_ℓ(G) at a high level, and you keep the scope to all graphs G, which matches the paper.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, define a k-list-assignment as a function L: V(G) → 2^N with |L(v)| = k for every vertex v.
Specify that an L-colouring c satisfies c(v) ∈ L(v) for every v ∈ V(G), and that it is proper when adjacent vertices receive different colours.
Specify that in the definition of χ^*_ℓ(G), the k proper colourings all come from the same k-list-assignment L.
State the disjointness condition explicitly as c_i(v) ≠ c_j(v) for every vertex v and every i ≠ j.
Use the paper’s term "L-packing of size k" for a collection of k pairwise-disjoint proper L-colourings.
The exact target in this paper is the specific factor-2 question in Problem 2.2, not the broader earlier conjecture that χ^*_ℓ is merely linearly bounded by χ_ℓ.
The paper does not separately state your second sentence as a proved equivalence; it is just the definitional unpacking of χ_ℓ(G) and χ^*_ℓ(G) from the surrounding context.
refined_question: For a graph G, let χ_ℓ(G) be the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment L: V(G) → 2^N admits a proper L-colouring, and let χ^*_ℓ(G) be the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment L of G admits an L-packing of size k, that is, k pairwise-disjoint proper L-colourings c_1, ..., c_k with c_i(v) ≠ c_j(v) for every v ∈ V(G) and every i ≠ j. Is it true that χ^*_ℓ(G) ≤ 2χ_ℓ(G) for every graph G?
justification: The nearest official formulation of your draft in arXiv:2411.10046 is Section 2, Problem 2.2 on page 3. The surrounding definitions on the same page introduce list-assignments, proper L-colourings, disjointness, χ_ℓ(G), and χ^*_ℓ(G), so those are the paper-faithful ingredients needed to make the question self-contained. The paragraph headed "The list packing conjecture" explains that the broader background is whether χ^*_ℓ is linearly bounded by χ_ℓ, but the paper then isolates the sharper factor-2 question as Problem 2.2; therefore your draft should be refined to that exact problem rather than broadened. I do not give a separate alternate formulation because the paper does not state one as an explicit proved equivalence.
